parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile national document/entry layer with a division that has no facility ban in force. National exposure is universal for outed travellers: X markers eliminated, sex-binary passport rules upheld, a visa cable directing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and considering lifetime fraud ineligibility, plus documented federal custody abuse (hormone removal, forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse). The division mitigates locally — its bathroom law was repealed, facility use is neither barred nor criminalised — but offers no statewide public-accommodation protection, no state hate-crime coverage for gender identity, and bars transition care in its custody. Violence data is an unusable undercount. Recourse exists but rules shift with litigation.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and directs consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers ended, markers only M/F; travellers report passports blocked or confiscated. Division's amended birth certificates must still display original assigned sex, feeding mismatch doubts.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa adjudication plus division ID-display rule interact: a corrected division document can still surface the original marker, raising the discrepancy trigger at any national checkpoint.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy for trans inmates (hair cut, hormones stopped, psychiatric substitution); documented abuse of trans men in immigration custody including forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; division bars state funds for transition care in prison.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Custody reporting of trans prisoners ceased in 2025; no division custody-placement or care protocol for visitors is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An ordinary visitor encounter (arrest, immigration hold) escalates into national custody where the hostile federal policy operates with division funding rules reinforcing care denial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility restrictions operate nationally in many units; a bathroom bill was revived in the division's 2025 session, leaving policy open to change within a legislative term.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division's 2016 birth-certificate bathroom rule was repealed 30 March 2017; no current statute bars or criminalises facility use matching gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Parent political momentum plus revived state bill mean the division's protective status is contingent, not settled, and could flip quickly.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s (2023) and bars state funds for transition care for minors and prisoners; national orders call minor care 'mutilation', freeze funding, and DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; visiting trans athletes barred from teams.
care_services.protection: Division imposes no care ban on adults; several national orders are enjoined or challenged in court.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor or accompanying parent faces care denial that litigation has not cured; custody removes even adult access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ reward memo lists 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist animating ideas; EO directs law enforcement to investigate schools promoting 'gender ideology'; advocates compare trajectory to genocide's early stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memo states rewards are not keyed to ideology alone and counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National rhetoric sets the climate division officers operate in, raising friction probability during any stop, though it is not itself a traveller-facing arrest power.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division's three 2023 laws end transition care under 18 and bar trans girls from teams; national EO threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; parents'-rights law requires schools to notify parents of name/pronoun requests.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented for a visiting minor; the school-focused provisions apply to institutions rather than visitors directly.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family trip with a trans minor loses care access, team participation and any privacy expectation, while an emergency would route into the same restricted system.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so bias assaults may go uncharged as bias; no statewide public-accommodation protection means service refusal has no statewide remedy; 3.0 killings/100k trans women is an acknowledged undercount with no baseline comparison and cannot be used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment-discrimination ruling and municipal ordinances in the largest city and one county (~30% of population) offer partial coverage.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Federal protection depends on enforcement while the state layer under-covers, so an outed visitor's remedy depends heavily on the specific city and county.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknown: county application of the original-marker display rule, licence interaction, 2025 bathroom bill text and enforcement, and geographic reach of local ordinances; national orders remain unresolved or enjoined, so rules shift between visits.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties litigation has previously repealed the division's facility law and removed a surgery requirement; national equality and identity-document maps track changes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation cuts both ways: courts have blocked some national measures while the passport regime was allowed to take effect, making timing decisive for any single trip.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars every visibly trans visitor at the border with unpublished criteria and no remedy. Here exclusion is document-discrepancy-triggered rather than identity-based, fraud findings are non-automatic with waivers, facility use is legal, and no registration or supervision regime exists. Entry exposure is real but narrower, so higher than 0.35-A.

Kestrel Isles shows secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow remedies — closely parallel to the national visa cable. This dossier adds documented custody abuse, a division custody care ban, no statewide accommodation or state hate-crime recourse, and majority public support for ASAB document rules, so somewhat lower than 0.55-B.

Meridia has trained officers, tribunal appeals and compensation for brief detention. Here document-mismatch refusal is mandated by cable, fraud ineligibility is considered, and division recourse for service or bias harm is thin. Considerably lower than 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two systems that interact rather than offset. At entry, the national document regime converts any mismatch into a discretionary refusal and possible permanent bar — a universal exposure for outed or outable visitors. Once inside the division, daily exposure is comparatively moderate: facility use is legal, the old bathroom law was repealed after sustained backlash, and federal employment and hate-crime protections persist. But that everyday latitude rests on thin division recourse — no statewide accommodation ban, no state bias classification for gender identity, patchy municipal coverage — and it collapses entirely in custody, where federal and division policies remove hormones and permit documented abuse. Litigation is active but unsettled; rules can change mid-itinerary. Net: moderate daily risk, sharp downside at border and custody stages.
